{{Quote|They're supposed to be geniuses at fixing and reassembling high-tech devices.|Luke Skywalker|<ref name="DFR">''[[Dark Force Rising]]''</ref>}}
The '''Verpine''' were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Insectoid/Legends|insectoid]] [[Species/Legends|species]] from the [[Roche asteroid field]]. Best known for their technological aptitude, the Verpine were considered to be among the finest [[Starship/Legends|starship]] [[Engineer/Legends|engineers]] in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|We are a literal people, Fett.|[[Sass Sikili]] to [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]]|<ref name="Sacrifice">''[[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Verpine2.0.jpg|thumb|left|170px|A Verpine.]]
Verpine were thin bipedal insectoids, standing 1.9 meters tall on average.<ref name="GG4" /> Unlike many insectoids, including the [[Kibnon/Legends|Kibnon]] to which they were distantly related,<ref name="Galaxy Guide 7: Mos Eisley">''[[Galaxy Guide 7: Mos Eisley]]'', 55.</ref> the Verpine had only four limbs (two arms and two legs), though there were instances of Verpine growing vestigial wings.<ref name="BH4" /> Their heads were dominated by large compound eyes. They also had two antennae, one located behind each eye. Their hardened carapace, composed of a green [[Chitin/Legends|chitinous]] substance called ''carahide'', was as flexible as the skin of other creatures, yet tough enough to deflect a blade or even absorb a glancing [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] bolt.<ref name="GG4" /> The Verpine circulatory system did not contain a heart — at least, not an organ which [[Human/Legends|Human]] physiologists would identify as a heart.<ref name="Star Wars 7">[[Star Wars (1977) 7|''Star Wars'' (1977) 7]]</ref>

Verpine eyes were keen enough to pick out microscopic details. Their antennae contained tympanic nerves which picked up sound. Their antennae were also sensitive to radio waves, giving Verpine the natural ability to sense and transmit radio waves to communicate with another Verpine in [[Verpine (language)|their language]] over distances on the order of one hundred kilometers. Some observers mistook this nearly instant, silent communication for true [[Telepathy/Legends|telepathy]]. Thanks to their natural radio communication network, their colonies were run as a consensus democracy, with all Verpine instantly consulted on questions affecting the hive.<ref name="GG4" />

Given their reliance on radio communication, Verpine frequently suffered negative consequences when their antenna were damaged. While researching the Verpine, [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] noticed that virtually all Verpine criminals suffered from a set of damaged antenna.<ref name="COPL">''[[The Courtship of Princess Leia]]''</ref>

Verpine came in two types&mdash;intelligent, [[Reproduction/Legends|hermaphroditic]] Verpine and unintelligent worker drones. At the time of their entrance into Galactic society, only five percent of Verpine were intelligent, but the demands of technological civilization required the Verpine to restructure their society. After the change, egg-laying Verpine used a special enzyme to ensure all eggs laid developed into intelligent Verpine. Any drones needed by a Verpine hive were produced via [[Cloning/Legends|cloning]].<ref name="GG4" />

When a Verpine hive needed more members, some of the fertile Verpine would be asked to lay eggs, while others would be assigned to fertilize them. The eggs were cared for in colony incubators, and hatchlings were cared for by the entire hive.<ref name="GG4" />

Some individual Verpine had [[Gender/Legends|genders]], either throughout their lifespan or at some point of their existences. A "hive mother" communicated with Jedi [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]] during the [[Swarm War]], and mentioned "male warriors."<ref name="Dark Nest III" /> [[General/Legends|General]] [[Airen Cracken/Legends|Airen Cracken]] referred to Moegid as "he" in his reports.<ref name="Cracken's Rebel Operatives">''[[Cracken's Rebel Operatives]]''</ref>

The fungus [[Magenge]], which grew inside the asteroid colonies of the Verpine, formed the basis of the Verpine diet.<ref name="Strike Force: Shantipole">''[[Strike Force: Shantipole]]''</ref>

==Society and culture==
[[File:Verpine_Tech_AoRSR.png|thumb|left|220px|A Verpine tech at work]]
Verpine had variable naming customs. Some had single names such as Fxz'et, Zix, Ss's,<ref name="UAA" /> or Moegid.<ref name="Vision">''[[Vision of the Future]]''</ref> Others had first and last names such as Kuli Ned'lx,<ref name="UAA" /> [[Kyli Ned'Ix]],<ref name="tdc">''[[The DarkStryder Campaign]]''</ref> or [[Osos Niskooen]].<ref name="Invincible">''[[Legacy of the Force: Invincible]]''</ref> Many, though not all, Verpine names contained sibilant consonants and glottal stops.<ref name="UAA" />

Verpines were also known to make highly sought after weapons such as the [[Verpine shatter gun]], the [[Verpine headband/Legends|Verpine headband]], and the [[Verpine prototype shield]].

Verpines normally counted in base six unlike humans who used base ten. The number twelve was known to a Verpine as "four fists".<ref name="XW:RS">''[[X-Wing: Rogue Squadron]]''</ref>

==History==
The Verpine people did not evolve in the asteroids of the [[Roche system]]. Each inhabited asteroid was only made livable through the creation of artificial, self-sustaining environments in the interior. Some observers thought that the Roche asteroids were the remains of a Verpine homeworld which had broken up either slowly through natural forces, or suddenly as a result of a catastrophic civil war. Others theorized that the Verpine were descended from [[Extragalactic/Legends|extra-galactic]] nomads who settled in the Roche asteroid field. The Verpine simply told outsiders that they did not know of the location of their original homeworld.<ref name="GG4" />

Whether it was due to the after-effects of this ancient civil war, or because of the political uniformity and egalitarianism of their civilization, the Verpine were a peaceful people, expert arbitrators who preferred compromise to conflict.<ref name="GG4" /> The large insects had long been a spacefaring race and had colonized the Roche asteroid belts before the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]] was born.<ref name="COPL" />

Following the [[Waymancy Storm]], Verpine master crafter [[Lyns Skutroo]] reverse-engineered the [[Sif-Alulan process]] used by the Waymancy weapons to develop the [[squintpipe process]]. This resulted in a brief period where rapid-firing [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolasers]] outclassed any available deflector shield across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], until [[7500s BBY]] when further developments in the squintpipe process resulted in stronger deflector shields.<ref name="Warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

By the time of the [[Jedi Civil War]], the Verpine were part of the [[Galactic community]]. High-quality Verpine-manufactured items ranging from [[Ion blaster/Legends|ion blasters]] to [[cardio-regulator]]s were widely used. Some of these designs were adapted and improved from other species, such as the [[Bothan/Legends|Bothans]] or the [[Arkanian/Legends|Arkanians]]. Contemporary rumors were suspicious of the Verpine, however. Extrapolating from the Verpine practice of testing ion blasters on active droids, some Verpine weapons and medical technology were thought to have been tested on live sentients.<ref name="KOTOR">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref>

In later years, Verpine engineering was exemplified by the starship manufacturer [[Slayn & Korpil/Legends|Slayn & Korpil]], which built the famous [[V-19 Torrent starfighter/Legends|V-19 Torrent starfighter]] for the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[A/SF-01 B-wing starfighter/Legends|B-wing starfighter]] for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]].<ref name="NEGVV">''[[The New Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]''</ref> Their shipbuilding skills were attributed to the need to produce vessels which could safely navigate the Roche asteroids.<ref name="GG4" /> The [[Roche Hive Mechanical Apparatus Design and Construction Activity for Those Who Need the Hive's Machines/Legends|Roche Hive Mechanical Apparatus Design and Construction Activity for Those Who Need the Hive's Machines]], more commonly known simply as "Roche", was a Verpine-owned [[Droid/Legends|droid]] manufacturer which met with limited success with models like the [[8D smelter droid]] and the [[J9 worker drone/Legends|J9 worker drone]].<ref name="NEGD">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref>

[[File:Duros-Verpine-Herglic.jpg|thumb|left|220px|A Duros mechanic works to repair a CZ-series droid]]
During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the Verpine were openly sympathetic towards the Rebel Alliance. However, they did not officially join the Rebellion as a whole, partly due to their natural pacifistic idealism,<ref name="GG4" /> and partly due to the Imperial "advisors" posted in their system. After the Empire fell, however, the Verpine became supporters of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], with a close relationship with its military.<ref name="AA">''[[Alien Anthology]]''</ref>

In [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]], the Verpines broke a number of contracts with the [[Barabel/Legends|Barabels]] to produce starships. They claimed that a "mad" hive mother had taken the ships, and given the nature of their society they were under no obligation to retrieve the ships. The Barabels did not see it in the same light, and began negotiating with [[Kubaz/Legends|Kubaz]] chefs for the sale of Verpine body parts to use in their cuisine. In response to this, the New Republic planned to send [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]] to mediate the situation. The situation deteriorated rapidly when a Barabel ship was discovered with frozen Verpine parts. A fleet was sent to avert a war between the species, and [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] herself traveled to mediate.<ref name="COPL" />

During the [[Swarm War]], some Verpine who were addicted to the [[Gorog]] Nest's [[Membrosia/Legends|black membrosia]] acted on the side of the [[Killik/Legends|Killiks]], including procuring B-wings and [[Verpine shatter gun]]s for the Killik forces. The Killiks attempted to invade the Verpine capital asteroid, [[Nickel One]], and overthrow their [[Verpine government|government]]. The attempt was foiled by the actions of the Jedi [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], [[Mara Jade Skywalker]] and [[Darth Caedus|Jacen Solo]].<ref name="Dark Nest III" />

[[File:SlicingIn-Hal.jpg|thumb|200px|Two Verpines infiltrating an Imperial complex]]
During the [[Second Galactic Civil War]], the Verpine accused the people of [[Murkhana/Legends|Murkhana]] of breaking trade agreements by producing technology similar to theirs. They signed a non-aggression pact with the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]] because of their fear that the Mandalorians would expand their borders once again and invade Verpine territory. The treaty was simple: the Mandalorians would supply their best export, military strength, while the Verpines would supply defense technology and quality control.<ref name="Sacrifice" />

This agreement was later put to the test when [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]] forces allied with [[Darth Caedus]] attacked the Verpine's home system in an attempt to gain control of their technology. The Mandalorians rushed to their aid and, with the help of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]], the Mandalorians [[Battle of Roche|fought to defend the system]].<ref name="Invincible" />

Following their experiences with Imperial attacks, the Verpine developed the [[IX-6 heavy combat droid]] to aid in their defense of the asteroid settlements.
Sometime after the establishment of [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire]] in [[130 ABY]], [[Roche asteroid field|Roche]] was ordered by Imperial officials to immediately cease the production of the IX-6 and destroy all existing models. Unwilling to succumb to the Empire, Verpine spread the factories throughout the Roche [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]] belt, hiding them deep in the asteroids which appeared abandoned from the surface. When the Empire learned of the defiance, a fleet of [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]] blasted several heavily populated Verpine asteroids to dust. The massacre, however, did not break the will of the Verpine species and Roche continued to produce new IX-6 and smuggle them to anyone who could afford them.<ref name="LECG">''[[Legacy Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

==Verpine in the galaxy==
[[File:Verpine_with_shatter_gun.jpg|thumb|left|The [[Verpine shatter gun]] was sold throughout the galaxy.]]
Many of the Verpine who left their home system found work as starship technicians. Most of them met with success, though some of them would get in trouble for continually making unauthorized, sometimes dangerous, "improvements" to the equipment they maintained. Others used their experience with Verpine communal decision making to act as professional arbitrators and negotiators.<ref name="GG4" /> At least one Verpine, [[Beyghor Sahdett]], became a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], and managed to survive [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]], killing a large number of [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] in the process.<ref name="SWR:IU">''[[Star Wars: Republic: Into the Unknown]]''</ref> A population of Verpine was present on the planet [[Essowyn]], where they were thought to be weak-willed by the native [[Saurton]]s.<ref name="PGV1">''[[Planets of the Galaxy, Volume One]]''</ref>

[[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] befriended a [[Pera|Verpine priest]] of the [[Sacred Way/Legends|Sacred Way]] on [[Aduba-3/Legends|Aduba-3]] after rescuing the clergyman from an angry mob.<ref name="SWG4">{{GamerCite|4|The Starhoppers of Aduba-3}}"</ref> Years later, Solo, [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]], and [[Lobot/Legends|Lobot]] worked with a Verpine [[Slicer/Legends|slicer]] named [[Moegid]] on an ill-fated mission to recover a copy of the [[Caamas Document]] from [[Bastion/Legends|Bastion]].<ref name="Vision" /> [[Zraii]], [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron's]] mechanic, was also a Verpine.<ref name="XW:RS" /> [[Suskafoo]], a member of the first hive contacted by the Alliance,<ref name="Strike Force: Shantipole" /> actively joined the Rebels by helping to develop the B-Wing and serving in [[Dagger Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Dagger Squadron]].<ref name="Star Wars: Rebellion 13: Small Victories, Part 3">[[Rebellion 13|''Rebellion'' 13]]</ref>

[[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton's]] [[LOM-series protocol droid/Legends|LOM-series protocol droids]], which had insectoid heads, were marketed toward insectoid species such as the Verpine.<ref name="EGTD">''[[The Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Buggie.jpg|thumb|right|upright|A "Buggie" priest on [[Aduba-3/Legends|Aduba-3]].]]
The insectoid priest Han Solo met in [[Star Wars (1977) 7|''Star Wars'' (1977) 7]] was not identified by species, though Solo referred to him as an "Insect-guy" and a "Buggie," with the latter nickname also being used by another character. The [[Retroactive continuity|retcon]] identifying the priest as a Verpine was established in [[Star Wars Gamer 4|''Star Wars Gamer'' 4]]. This character has a yellow-green exoskeleton and large green eyes, but no visible antennae. The priest was also addressed as "Pera", meaning "Father" in [[High Galactic (language)|High Galactic]].

It is possible that "Buggie" is a common nickname for Verpines&mdash;possibly a derogatory one, since Solo used the more respectful "Pera" when addressing the priest directly. According to [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]] in ''[[Dark Nest I: The Joiner King]]'', Solo had been uncomfortable with insectoid species since his encounter with [[Kamarian]]s (as seen in ''[[Han Solo's Revenge]]'').
